batumi_centre_about.title: About the Centre

callout.text: CLOSED for renovation. No confirmed reopening date — please call ahead to check. The coordinator has been told 1 November 2026 as a schedule target, but this is not confirmed and could change.

batumi_centre_about.note: Run by Sailors' Society Batumi with the local seafarers' rights council. Closed 1–2 Jan, 7 Jan, 24 Apr, 26 May — on top of the current renovation. Hours above are what applies once it reopens.

batumi_centre_services.title: Services
batumi_centre_services.note: No hot meals cooked — tea, coffee and snacks only. All of this is on hold while the centre is closed for renovation.

batumi_centre_location.title: Location & Route

directions.title: From Checkpoint No.1 (passenger): ~450 m, 6 min
directions.sub: Turn right onto Gogoberashvili St. — the centre is on your left

directions.title: From Checkpoint No.2 (cargo/oil): ~150 m, 2 min
directions.sub: Exit straight onto Gogoberashvili St. — the centre is 150 m on your right

directions.title: From Checkpoint No.3 (industrial): ~1.2 km, 15 min, or 3 min by taxi
directions.sub: Along Mayakovski St. to Baku St., then to Gogoberashvili St.

batumi_centre_location.note: Avoid the unlit railway tracks near Checkpoint No.3 — use the Baku St. pavement instead.

callout.text: Yes — shore leave is normally permitted at Batumi. Always confirm with your Master or ship's agent before you go.

batumi_transport_leaving.note: All checkpoints operate 24/7. For problems, call your agent or the port duty officer: +995 422 27 60 15.

batumi_transport_taxi.title: Taxi

rows.title: Right outside Checkpoint No.1 or No.2

batumi_transport_taxi.note: 5–10 GEL (~$2–4) into the centre. Unofficial drivers: no roof sign, no taxi sticker, no yellow/white plate, quote a price before you even get in, don't use an app, and ask for cash upfront — walk past them. Always fix the price in GEL before getting in, or use an app. Don't pay street drivers in USD or EUR.

batumi_transport_public.title: Public Transport

rows.title: "Gogoberashvili St. / Cable Car Station"
rows.sub: ~200 m from the checkpoints

rows.title: Buses 1, 1a, 2, 4, 10, 15
rows.sub: No.10 also runs to the airport, along the boulevard

batumi_transport_public.note: 5–10 minutes to the centre, 0.80 GEL. Cash is NOT accepted on buses — contactless international card (Visa/Mastercard), the Georgian transport card, or Apple/Google Pay only. Last buses run about 23:00–23:30.

callout.text: Never exchange money on the street, even for a good rate someone offers you. In some countries this is a criminal offence — and it's one of the most common ways seafarers get scammed near a port.

rows.title: A stranger offers you a better rate
rows.sub: On the street, at the gate, or "just around the corner" — always a scam

rows.title: Being asked to go somewhere private
rows.sub: A car, a back room, an alley — a legitimate exchange never needs this

rows.title: No receipt offered
rows.sub: A real exchange always gives you a printed receipt with the rate used

rows.title: Know the rough official rate first
rows.sub: Check on your phone before you go — so you can spot a bad deal immediately

rows.title: Count what you receive, before you walk away
rows.sub: In front of the person who gave it to you, not after
